captions.detailed: This 3D model is a custom corner-mounting protective cover designed to shield exposed screw terminals on a power supply. It features an L-shaped mounting flange with pre-drilled screw holes for wall attachment, leading to a vertical protective plate patterned with rows of small diamond-shaped ventilation slots. On one side, a deep circular cutout and a chamfered bottom corner allow for clean routing of thick power cables.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD script for a power supply terminal corner cover. The design must include adjustable parameters for wall thickness, power supply width and height, distance from the wall, and cover height, featuring mounting screw holes, an array of diamond-shaped ventilation holes, and customized cable entry cutouts.
captions.factory: The design uses a difference() block to subtract cutouts from a union() of several plates and cylinders. The main plates are generated using cube() primitives positioned with translate(). Cylindrical rods (cylinder() with rotate() and translate()) are added to reinforce the internal corners. A nested for-loop subtracts 4-sided cylinders ($fn=4) rotated to form diamond-shaped air vents, while additional cylinders subtract screw holes and circular/chamfered wire cutouts.
